title: Two Kepler months show an amplitude gap in 29 tested steady target-mode alias bands
abstract: We test whether single steady fast modes on KIC 10001893 can give its known 19.48-hour signal through long-cadence sampling. We reuse two Kepler release-25 short-cadence months and fit 1,379 frequencies in 29 bands, from the first sampling order to the short-cadence Nyquist limit. We compare nominal noise radii with the amplitudes needed to produce a 29-ppm long-cadence alias after frame integration and conservative target dilution. The largest radius-to-required-amplitude ratio is 0.171, or 0.144 in aperture flux. This extends a prior one-band test to both branches and higher orders. It argues against these steady target-mode aliases under a linear response and the stated noise assumptions. Estimated block covariances do not give exact confidence coverage. Variable modes, multiple modes, blends, nonlinear response and frequencies between grid points remain open. No planet or new source is confirmed. Code, aggregate results, a figure, exact input hashes and separate-storage retrieval steps are included.

display.caption: Nominal upper amplitude radius divided by the required target amplitude in 29 tested alias bands. Values below one show an amplitude gap under the stated model and noise assumptions.
